audits.title: Mammography rates for 20 community-based family practices in Ontario: a full practice audit.
audits.standard: Mammogram every two years for women aged 50 to 69

cycle1.result: Two-year time-appropriate mammography rate 58.8% (range 25% to 76%); four practices reached 70% or more.

audits.other_findings: Rate rose to 70.0% with a 36-month window; no practice factor was associated with screening rate.
audits.citation: Swanson JG, Kaczorowski J. Mammography rates for 20 community-based family practices in Ontario: a full practice audit. Can J Public Health. 2007;98(5):374-378. doi:10.1007/bf03405422. PMID: 17985678.

audits.title: Chart Audit of Mammography in a Family Practice: How to improve screening rates with a chart audit and outreach.
audits.standard: Mammography within 2 years for women aged 50 to 69
audits.intervention: Outreach by mail and telephone to women without a mammogram.
audits.other_findings: Pap smear within 2 years and history of breast lumps were associated with mammography.
audits.citation: Yaphe J, Sangster J, Guthrie J. Chart Audit of Mammography in a Family Practice: How to improve screening rates with a chart audit and outreach. Can Fam Physician. 1992;38:2314-2317. PMID: 21221291.

audits.title: Mammography Adherence: Creation of a Process Change Plan to Increase Usage Rates.
audits.setting: Clinic at Palmetto Health, South Carolina Cancer Center, Columbia; nurse-led QI
audits.intervention: Staff communication about problems, streamlined referral process, scripted message, up-front assessment of financial and social barriers and early referral to resources.
audits.citation: Smalls TE, Heiney SP, Baliko B, Tavakoli AS. Mammography Adherence: Creation of a Process Change Plan to Increase Usage Rates. Clin J Oncol Nurs. 2019;23(3):281-287. doi:10.1188/19.cjon.281-287. PMID: 31099801.

audits.title: Improving Breast Cancer Screening Coverage in Primary Healthcare: A Quality-Improvement Study (2023-2025).
audits.standard: Target coverage of at least 76% of eligible women aged 40-69 by September 2025; diagnostic follow-up ≤14 days
audits.setting: Primary healthcare network, Armed Forces Hospital, Dhahran
audits.intervention: Four PDSA cycles: staff awareness, EHR-generated eligibility lists and recall, dashboards and feedback, workflow integration with periodic audits
audits.other_findings: 1,652 mammograms completed with 11 confirmed malignancies; waiting times improved after capacity adjustments.
audits.citation: AlAwadh SA, AlShammari RZ, AlJohi HA, Aseeri RM, AlOhali FT, Alghamdi AM, et al.. Improving Breast Cancer Screening Coverage in Primary Healthcare: A Quality-Improvement Study (2023-2025). Cureus. 2026;18(5):e108674. doi:10.7759/cureus.108674. PMID: 42281707.

audits.title: Use of a Paper Checklist to Increase Clinician Adherence to Mammography Screening Guidelines.
audits.standard: American Cancer Society mammography screening guidelines
audits.intervention: Screening checklist completed by the woman at registration and given to the clinician during the examination.

cycle2.result: Mammogram recommended and ordered for 69.6% of women (p = .01).

audits.other_findings: Authors recommend a paperless system as adherence still needs improvement.
audits.citation: Cox AL, Heiney SP, Baliko B. Use of a Paper Checklist to Increase Clinician Adherence to Mammography Screening Guidelines. Nurs Womens Health. 2020;24(4):277-282. doi:10.1016/j.nwh.2020.05.003. PMID: 32663442.
